title: Effect of a Trace Addition of Sn on the Aging Behavior of Al–Mg–Si Alloy with a Different Mg/Si Ratio

pre_treatment.processing: Section 2: "The as-cast ingots were homogenized at 540 °C for 30 h. ... hot rolled from 42 mm to 7 mm at 480 °C. The hot rolled slabs were annealed at 420 °C for 2 h and then cold-rolled down to a thickness of 1 mm."
pre_treatment.solution_treatment: Section 2: "Solution heat treatment of the cold-rolled sheets were performed at 570 °C for 30 min, followed by water quenching to room temperature."
pre_treatment.natural_ageing_delay: Not stated in the paper (no delay between quench and 180 °C ageing is specified). DSC was run on as-quenched specimens.
pre_treatment.hardness_method: Section 2: "HV-10B Vickers hardness tester with a load of 4.9 N and indention time of 10 s ... average value of five indentations."
pre_treatment.dsc_method: Section 2: "The DSC curves of the as-quenched specimens were tested by the DSC-700 instrument ... heated from room temperature to 500 °C with the heating rate of 10 °C/min."

expected_sign.peak_hardness_HV: higher hardness with a more negative predicted energy: agreement = -tau

expected_sign.dsc_beta_dprime_peak_C: lower beta'' peak temperature with a more negative predicted energy: agreement = +tau

mapping_rule: item = alloy; donor prediction = that donor's formation energy (eV/atom) of the most stable Mg- and Si-containing candidate whose atomic Mg/Si ratio is closest (in log ratio) to the alloy's; at% from Table 1 wt% with Al as balance

caveats: Six alloys but only three distinct Mg/Si ratios (1.68, 1.00, 0.58) at constant Mg+Si about 1.6 wt%; three of the six carry 0.10-0.11 wt% Sn, a second variable. The Sn-free subset (H–M, B–M, L–M) is the clean Mg/Si series.
Natural-ageing delay before 180 °C ageing is not reported.
Ageing-time resolution: peak times are as stated by the authors from discrete hardness sampling (Figure 1).
